text: In Mathura, the wedding of Devaki and Vasudeva was celebrated in great splendour.
Kamsa, Devaki's own brother, loved his sister so dearly that he drove her chariot himself.
But midway through that journey an akashavani — a voice from the sky — was heard: “The eighth child born to Devaki will be the cause of your death.”
And that was all it took… fear closed over the love he had for his sister.
Kamsa moved to kill Devaki then and there.
Vasudeva stopped him and gave his word: “Every child born to Devaki, I will hand over to you.”
Even so, Kamsa imprisoned Devaki and Vasudeva.
Time passed.
One by one, Kamsa killed the children born to Devaki.
A mother losing her children… a father watching, able to do nothing… and in that prison cell the years went by.
At last… the time came for the eighth child to be born.
Ashtami tithi.
The hour of midnight.
Outside, everything was darkness… but that prison cell alone filled with a divine light.
To Devaki, Sri Mahavishnu himself came — born as Sri Krishna.
That was no ordinary birth of a child.
It was the moment dharma was born in the middle of adharma.
The moment light came in the middle of darkness.
The instant Krishna was born, a wonder happened.
The prison doors opened of their own accord.
The guards fell into deep sleep.
Vasudeva's chains slipped away.
Vasudeva placed the little Krishna in a basket… and that very night set out from Mathura for Gokulam.
Outside, heavy rain.
The river Yamuna was in flood.
His little one above his head… the swelling Yamuna before him… and still Vasudeva did not take a single step back.
Adishesha spread his hoods and followed, sheltering Balakrishna from the rain.
And Yamunamma too rose up for the touch of little Krishna's feet… longing to touch those small feet, she gave way and made a path for Vasudeva's journey.
At last Vasudeva reached the house of Nanda and Yashodamma in Gokulam.
There, a baby girl had just been born to Yashodamma.
Vasudeva left Balakrishna there… took that baby girl, and returned to the prison in Mathura.
In the morning Kamsa learned that a child had been born.
As he tried to kill her… she slipped from his hands, took on a divine form, and warned him: “The one who will destroy you is already born, elsewhere.”
And in Gokulam… Yashodamma alone did not know who it was she held in her lap.
Did not know he was the protector of the worlds.
Did not know he had come to end adharma.
Did not know he was Sri Mahavishnu himself.
To her he was not God… he was her own little Kannayya.
He ate butter from her hand.
He slept in her lap.
He stole butter from the gopikas' houses.
In Nanda's home he filled the days with his laughter and his mischief.
The Paramatma who had come to protect the world… grew up as a small boy in a mother's lap.
The Krishna who was born as God in Mathura… in Gokulam, through love, became “our own Kannayya”.
Jai Sri Krishna
Govinda… Gopala…
